item.title: This week on "Sunday Morning" (Aug. 9)
item.description: A look at the features for this week's broadcast of the Emmy-winning program, hosted by Jane Pauley.

item.title: Iran says strait won't open until the U.S. "corrects" behavior
item.description: The United Arab Emirates' Abu Dhabi National Oil Company said one of its ships was targeted while transiting the strait on Saturday.

item.title: Senate confirms Todd Blanche, Trump's ex-defense lawyer, as attorney general
item.description: In a narrow 50-49 vote, President Trump's former defense lawyer was confirmed as attorney general in a vote early Saturday.

item.title: The family-owned business turning walls into works of art
item.description: A family-owned wallpaper company made luxury design their booming business. Meg Oliver takes a look inside Phillip Jeffries, the decor business turning walls into works of art.

item.title: Exclusive discounts from CBS Mornings Deals
item.description: On this edition of CBS Deals, we show you items that will help improve your everyday lifestyle. Visit cbsdeals.com to take advantage of these exclusive deals today. CBS earns commissions on purchases made through cbsdeals.com.

item.title: Instagram owner Meta ordered to pay nearly $1B in fines for risking child safety, court says
item.description: Meta, the parent company of Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and others, must pay nearly $1 billion after a court found the social media giant to have put children and teen users at risk. A New Mexico judge ruled that Meta must pay $567 million into a fund to pay for harm prevention and awareness, in addition to $375 million in civil penalties previously decided by a jury.

item.title: Saturday Sessions: Houndmouth performs "Never Gonna Die"
item.description: Indiana rock band Houndmouth is acclaimed for their rich harmonies and electric live performances. Their latest record, "Lordy," is a stripped-back, raw return, five years after their last album. Here's Houndmouth with "Never Gonna Die."

item.description: Indiana rock band Houndmouth is acclaimed for their rich harmonies and electric live performances. Their latest record, "Lordy," is a stripped-back, raw return, five years after their last album. Here's Houndmouth with "Heavy Eyes."

item.title: World-class dining collides with boutique Bohemian style in SERRE at The Maker Hotel
item.description: A lush glass conservatory has been converted into a dining room at SERRE, a boutique hotel restaurant nestled in New York's Hudson Valley. Chef Jonas Offenbach puts a modern twist on classic French techniques to bring delicious plates to diners inside of this experience at The Maker Hotel.

item.title: Wildfires in western Canada forces more than 20,000 people to evacuate
item.description: The Bald Range wildfire was first reported on Friday evening.

item.title: Jorge Messi, father of Argentina great Lionel Messi, dies at 68
item.description: Jorge Messi served as his son's agent and accompanied him to Europe when he signed with Barcelona as a teenager.

item.title: Kevin Sussman reprises "The Big Bang Theory" role in "Stuart Fails to Save the Universe"
item.description: Kevin Sussman is back as Stuart Bloom, a comic book store owner who fans first met on "The Big Bang Theory." Sussman explains what lies ahead for his iconic character in "Stuart Fails to Save the Universe."

item.title: Europeans face energy crisis as heat wave brings wildfires and drought
item.description: The Danube River hasn't been this low in over 200 years. Wildfires are scorching multiple countries in Europe. Less water means less nuclear energy generation, bringing an energy crisis. Ramy Inocencio details Europe's heat wave struggles.

item.title: These are the "super scooper" firefighting seaplanes dousing European and U.S. wildfires
item.description: As wildfires rage in parts of the United States and Europe, firefighting efforts have taken to the seas and skies. CBS Saturday Morning takes a look at these remarkable "super scooper" amphibious aircraft.

item.title: Puerto Rico's mismanaged, broken infrastructure worsens drought impact
item.description: Puerto Rico has entered a period of water rationing as existing infrastructure issues worsen the impact of an ongoing drought. While government officials focus on the lack of rain, residents point to government mismanagement and underfunded, aging infrastructure as the source of many ongoing issues, from water shortages to years of rolling blackouts. Lilia Luciano has more context.

item.title: How to handle healthcare expenses after retiring
item.description: Some older Americans find themselves at a loss when it comes to managing healthcare expenses after retirement starts. Jill Schlesinger has tips on how to stay healthy after retiring.

item.title: Harrowing police footage shows gunman's deadly rampage at Idaho In-N-Out Burger
item.description: Three people were killed during a shooting that began at an In-N-Out restaurant in Twin Falls, Idaho. The gunman died of a self-inflicted gunshot wound, police said. Investigators have now released security footage as they probe the motive for the shooting.

item.title: Police warn of dangerous "video game style" driving
item.description: Driving like a "Grand Theft Auto" player in real life is both illegal and highly dangerous, police warn. Kris Van Cleave went on a ride-along to see what the California Highway Patrol is dealing with.

item.title: Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey sign defense pact as Iran repeats that Hormuz deal is close
item.description: Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey signed a historic joint defense pact, establishing their mutual support in case of an attack. Meanwhile, Iran said again that it is finalizing a deal to co-manage the Strait of Hormuz with Oman.

item.title: Todd Blanche narrowly confirmed as attorney general
item.description: The Senate narrowly confirmed President Trump's former defense lawyer, Todd Blanche, as the U.S. Attorney General. Republicans Sens. Susan Collins of Maine and Lisa Murkowski of Alaska joined Democrats in voting against Blanche's nomination to serve as the nation's top law enforcement official.

item.title: U.S. pledges $1 billion to Colombia as new right-wing president takes office
item.description: Abelardo de la Espriella, a millionaire lawyer with a taste for spectacle, took office Friday.

item.title: Powerball grows to highest jackpot of the year
item.description: The total is also the eighth-largest Powerball jackpot in the game's history.

item.title: Girl dies from injuries after school shooting in Thailand as death toll rises
item.description: Five school staff members died in the shooting outside Bangkok. The shooter also appeared to have killed his two grandparents.

item.title: Senate approves bill to fund government into December
item.description: The measure was approved in a 90 to 6 vote and now goes to the House.

item.title: Man has "miracle" recovery after heart defect causes rare massive stroke
item.description: One year after a massive stroke nearly incapacitated him, Todd Meiklejohn is opening up about his experience.

item.title: Child among 4 people killed in Russian attacks on Ukraine
item.description: Falling debris sparked several fires on the outskirts of the Ukrainian capital, in attacks which killed at least four people

item.title: 8/8: CBS Saturday Morning
item.description: Todd Blanche is confirmed as attorney general, fires blaze in Europe and the U.S., plus Houndmouth plays Saturday Sessions.

item.title: The Uplift: Hot ones
item.description: Vladimir Duthiers meets Sean Evans, host of "Hot Ones," the online show that has celebrities answer questions while attempting to eat chicken wings that get progressively spicier. Can Vlad stand the heat?

item.title: Helicopter fighting massive Utah wildfire crashes, no word on 2 people aboard
item.description: The Federal Aviation Administration confirmed that the helicopter crashed in Richfield, which is about 160 miles south of Salt Lake City.
